scope: Theorem 14 (Transfer through small supports) of the manuscript “Choiceless polynomial time with counting does not capture polynomial time” (preprints/Choiceless-polynomial-time-with-counting-does-not-capture-polynomial-time-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 243 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3e16a83bb7707c83), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 19. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let A0, A1 be nonempty finite structures in the same binary relational vocabulary, and let Ki ≤ Aut(Ai) for i ∈ {0, 1}. Let s, m, M be positive integers satisfying max{4, m + 1}s ≤ M. Assume the following two properties. 1. A0 and A1 satisfy the same CM sentences. 2. In each Ai, any two tuples of length at most max{2, m}s with the same CM type lie in the same Ki orbit. For i ∈ {0, 1}, let Di consist of the objects x in HF(Ai) such that x and every object in its transitive closure have a Ki-support of length at most s. Equip Di with membership, an atom predicate, and the relations of Ai, interpreted as false on arguments containing a non-atom. Then D0 and D1 satisfy the same Cm sentences.
